title: Some Trust in Chariots: A Prayer for the King
summary: The people pray for their king on the day of trouble, asking the LORD to answer him, send help from Zion, accept his offerings, and grant his plans. A single voice then declares confidence that the LORD saves his anointed. The psalm sets those who trust in chariots and horses against those who trust in the name of the LORD, and ends with a plea for God to save the king.

from.where: The Study Bible's introduction to the Psalms
from.text: Royal psalms are about the king of Israel: his crowning, his wedding, his battles, God's promise to his family (Psalms 2, 18, 20, 21, 45, 72, 89, 101, 110, 132, 144).

line: The people pray for their king in the day of trouble, and the psalm sets those who trust in chariots and horses against those who trust the name of the LORD.
guide: Name your own chariots: money, health, skill, a plan. None of them is evil; the psalm asks what you trust when trouble comes. Use it to pray for leaders by name, before their hard days.

stanzas.title: The people's prayer for the king on the day of trouble
Now I know: the LORD saves his anointed
Chariots and horses, or the name of the LORD

verses.t: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David. May the LORD answer you in the day of trouble; may the name of the God of Jacob protect you.
May He send you help from the sanctuary and sustain you from Zion.
May He remember all your gifts and look favorably on your burnt offerings. Selah
May He give you the desires of your heart and make all your plans succeed.
May we shout for joy at your victory and raise a banner in the name of our God. May the LORD grant all your petitions.
Now I know that the LORD saves His anointed; He answers him from His holy heaven with the saving power of His right hand.
Some trust in chariots and others in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God.
They collapse and fall, but we rise up and stand firm.
O LORD, save the king. Answer us on the day we call.
